text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- B BAND WILL RAISE 3.7 BILLION PLUS PREMIUM
The Brazilian government will rake in at least 3.69 billion reais through the offer of concessions to operate cellular services on the B Band frequency.
-- ORANGE JUICE AND SOY FUTURES PRICES RISE
The prices for orange juice and soybean futures yesterday rose 2.4 percent and one percent respectively as a result of frost fears in Florida and a decline in soybean output in the United States.
-- 400 TRUCKS STRANDED IN URUGUAY BY CUSTOMS
Some 400 trucks loaded with foods, mostly meats and grains, are awaiting permission to enter Brazil through Uruguayan customs on the border with Argentina because they lack import licenses.
O GLOBO
-- CARDOSO INSISTS PMDB PARTY VOTE ON RE-ELECTION
President Fernando Henrique Cardoso gave the PMDB party an ultimatum yesterday: vote on re-election or leave the government alliance. "I was betrayed and I'm not going to accept that," he said.
-- FEDERAL BANK WILL FINANCE HOME LOAN REPAYMENTS

The federal bank Caixa Economica Federal will create new mechanisms to serve as incentives for the repayment of home financing as the results of a programme launched in September were worse than expected.
-- MARIJUANA WAS STORED IN GRAVE IN RIO
Police found half a ton of marijuana stored in a tomb at the English Cemetery at Rio de Janeiro's Gamboa district. The drug stash belonged to traffickers in the city's Portuario district.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- CARDOSO THREATENS PMDB TO GET IT TO VOTE ON RE-ELECTION

President Fernando Henrique Cardoso on Monday threatened the PMDB, the biggest party in Congress, to get it to vote today on a constitutional amendment that would allow him to run for re-election in 1998.
-- UNEMPLOYMENT HITS RECORD UNDER REAL ECONOMIC PLAN

Some 176,142 jobs were lost in Sao Paulo's industrial sector in 1996 for a jobs-loss rate of 8.17 percent, raising to 320,864 the number of posts eliminated since Brazil instituted its Real economic plan in mid-1994.
-- FUEL PRICES RAISE INFLATION RATE IN SAO PAULO
Inflation in Sao Paulo rose to 0.78 percent in the four-week period ended January 7, up from 0.17 percent in December, according to the Economic Research Institute (Fipe).
Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
-- James Craig, Sao Paulo newsroom 5511 232 4411
